summary: Initial security posture discovery with Haven Health. Customer is evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for PHI-adjacent workloads. Key concerns: SOC 2/ISO certifications, SSO (SAML/Okta), RBAC, audit logs retention, encryption and KMS/HSM options, data residency, and egress. Redwood AE/SE outlined deployment options, network/topology choices, KMS integration and audit capabilities. Agreed next steps: share SOC2/ISO artifacts, schedule private deployment demo, customer to send network diagram and regulatory checklist.
topics: Encryption at rest and in transit / KMS / HSM
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-26
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendez (CISO, Haven Health), Lina Park (Head of Platform), Samir Patel (DevOps), Maya Torres (Legal)

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick intros?
[00:10] Carlos Mendez: Yeah hi, Carlos here, CISO at Haven. Our main reason for this call is to understand Redwood's security posture — we run PHI-adjacent workloads, so SOC2, encryption, key management and SSO are must-haves.
[00:25] Jordan Lee: Totally, that's what we want to cover. Priya, I think you can jump into the technical parts.
[00:29] Priya Raman: Sure, thanks. Quick agenda: certifications, identity and access, logging/audit, encryption/KMS, networking and data residency, then Q&A. Does that work?
[00:37] Lina Park: Works for me.
[00:38] Samir Patel: Yep.
[00:40] Priya Raman: Great. On certifications — Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001. We can provide the report and summary. For Hosted customers we maintain the compliance scope on our managed service; for Dedicated and Private deployments customers have options for additional attestations depending on contract.
[01:05] Carlos Mendez: When you say "scope", does that include access controls and logging for customer data? We need separation for Prod data and the ability to demonstrate controls for auditors.
[01:15] Priya Raman: Yes, for Hosted our control environment covers the platform and we provide audit logs, RBAC, SSO, and configurable retention windows. For Dedicated you get a reserved cluster and we still include those features but with more isolation — and for Private, the control plane can be customer-managed so your auditors can review environment more directly.
[01:34] Jordan Lee: To add — many enterprises go Dedicated first as a hybrid step; they want the predictability and isolation with Redwood managing the runtime, whereas Private is more for full on-prem or VPC-managed deployments where you control keys and network.
[01:46] Carlos Mendez: Ok, can you clarify KMS options? We require customer-managed keys for certain datasets, ideally HSM-backed.
[01:55] Priya Raman: Absolutely. For Hosted we support customer-managed KMS — integration with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault. We also support HSM-backed keys via customer KMS where available. For Dedicated we can allow a KMS integration per-tenant; for Private you bring your own KMS/HSM since you control the control plane. Key rotation, audit logs for key usage, and envelope encryption are supported.
[02:22] Samir Patel: Is key usage logged and surfaced in the console or via API? We need to feed to our SIEM.
[02:28] Priya Raman: Yes logs are emitted — we push audit events (key-access, model loads, admin actions) to CloudWatch/Stackdriver or via syslog/Splunk connectors; we can also provide a secure log export for retention policies.
[02:42] Maya Torres: From a legal perspective, we need to see data retention and deletion guarantees. How do you handle retention for prompts, completions, and embedding vectors?
[02:52] Jordan Lee: Good question. By default Redwood Hosted has configurable retention windows; we can set short retention for prompts/responses or opt-in to longer retention for evals. For customers with strict requirements we recommend Dedicated/Private — Dedicated can be configured to avoid long-term storage by default; Private gives you full control. We'll share the retention policy doc.
[03:12] Lina Park: Do you allow disabling of training/usage for Hosted? We can't have customer data used for model training.
[03:18] Priya Raman: Yes — we have an "opt-out of model training" flag for enterprise agreements. Hosted enterprise customers can opt out and we have contractual language to that effect.
[03:28] Carlos Mendez: Good. Another item is identity — we use Okta and expect SAML SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and SSO enforcement with MFA.
[03:36] Jordan Lee: We support SSO via SAML and OIDC; SCIM provisioning is supported for user sync, and we enforce RBAC layered on top. We also integrate with IdP MFA.
[03:46] Priya Raman: For RBAC we have role templates (admin, developer, viewer, auditor) and custom roles. RBAC can be scoped to orgs, projects and routes. We also provide token-level permissions and API keys with fine-grained scopes.
[04:05] Samir Patel: Any rate-limiting or token rotation best-practices? We want to programmatically rotate keys.
[04:10] Priya Raman: Yes, API keys are revokable and we recommend short TTLs with automation for rotation. We also support OAuth flows for service accounts and mTLS for private peered endpoints.
[04:22] Speaker 1: (inaudible) KV cache was mentioned earlier — does that have any customer-facing PII concerns?
[04:30] Priya Raman: I think the question is about KV cache / prefix caching. We don't persist client-specific KV to long-term storage for Hosted unless configured for performance; it's treated similarly to request caching and can be disabled. For Dedicated/Private you can configure cache persistence policies.
[04:50] Carlos Mendez: Audit logs — what's the retention window and can we export logs to our SIEM for the length we require? Regulators expect 7 years for some records.
[04:59] Priya Raman: By default audit logs are retained for 90 days in the console, but we support exporting to customer S3 with lifecycle policies. For Hosted we can arrange longer retention via add-on; Dedicated/Private gives you full control to retain as long as you need because logs can be routed to your storage.
[05:18] Lina Park: Data residency — we operate in EU and US, some data must remain in EU. Do you support regional control?
[05:26] Jordan Lee: Yes — regional deployments are supported. Hosted provides region selection for tenant data; Dedicated offers a regional cluster and Private you run in your VPC region. We can also help with data egress controls and contractual clauses.
[05:38] Carlos Mendez: Ok, network topology examples? We'd like to see what a VPC peering vs private control plane looks like.
[05:46] Priya Raman: We'll share diagrams. Briefly: VPC peering -> Redwood-managed control plane with peered data plane in your VPC; Private -> you run both control and data planes in your network or on-prem; Dedicated -> Redwood manages a customer-dedicated pool with isolated tenancy, typically in a customer-preferred region and with network ACLs.
[06:05] Jordan Lee: Many customers start Hosted for dev/test and then Dedicated for production, or go Private if they need full on-prem compliance.
[06:12] Samir Patel: Regarding ingress/egress, does Redwood allow restricting outbound connections from the model runtime? We need strict egress controls for PHI.
[06:21] Priya Raman: Yes. For Dedicated and Private you can lock down egress via VPC controls, egress rules, and firewall policies. Hosted has more managed egress but we can work with customers on allowed destinations and IP whitelists.
[06:35] Carlos Mendez: Encryption at rest — are data and model artifacts encrypted? How about ephemeral disk for the runtime?
[06:42] Priya Raman: All storage is encrypted at rest. For Hosted we use provider-managed disk encryption plus envelope encryption with customer KMS optionally. Ephemeral runtime storage is encrypted and zeroed on teardown.
[06:56] Maya Torres: Do you provide attestation or a security questionnaire? We'll need to run this past our procurement and legal.
[07:03] Jordan Lee: Yes, we can provide a completed security questionnaire, SOC2 report and ISO summary. We'll also provide contact for support and compliance.
[07:12] Priya Raman: Also for technical reviewers we'll set up a private demo environment so you can see audit logs, RBAC, SSO flows and KMS usage.
[07:22] Carlos Mendez: That would be ideal. We want to validate the logging pipeline and key access logs.
[07:27] Priya Raman: Understood.
[07:30] Jordan Lee: Quick pause — any non-security blockers like cost or latency concerns?
[07:35] Lina Park: Latency is a factor — some of our products are latency-sensitive. We'll need to see benchmarks for low-latency models plus cost tradeoffs.
[07:44] Jordan Lee: We can run a benchmark on Dedicated. Priya can scope that.
[07:48] Priya Raman: Yes, as part of pilot we can run a throughput/latency benchmark and give recommended batch sizes, quantization and caching policies.
[07:55] Samir Patel: For the private demo, we'll need network allowlist IP ranges and ports.
[07:59] Jordan Lee: We'll include that in the network diagram package.
[08:05] Speaker 2: (crosstalk) Are there assumptions about customer-managed keys and backups?
[08:10] Priya Raman: If you bring your own KMS, backup and key rotation are under your control; we record usage events and can surface them in audit logs.
[08:18] Carlos Mendez: Can you speak to pen tests and vulnerability scans?
[08:22] Priya Raman: Redwood runs quarterly vulnerability scans and annual pen tests; we share summaries with customers under NDA and have a coordinated disclosure policy.
[08:33] Maya Torres: For contractual language we'll need indemnity and liability clauses around data breaches.
[08:38] Jordan Lee: That's handled during procurement and we can loop in Legal; we'll include standard contract language and can discuss specific adjustments as needed.
[08:47] Carlos Mendez: One more technical — does Redwood support hardware-based isolation for multi-tenant workloads?
[08:54] Priya Raman: We use tenant isolation mechanisms; Dedicated provides isolated tenancy and private pools on GPU hosts. For Hosted, we use strong logical isolation and process-level safeguards. If you need hardware-backed isolation we can discuss Private/on-prem where you manage the hardware.
[09:12] Jordan Lee: Should we walk through a proposed timeline and next steps?
[09:16] Carlos Mendez: Yes please.
[09:18] Jordan Lee: Proposed: Redwood to share SOC2 docs and ISO summary (Jordan/Priya); Priya to schedule a technical deep dive/demo for Private deployment (Priya); Samir to send network diagram and whitelist; Maya to compile legal/regulatory checklist. After the deep dive we can provision a pilot Dedicated environment for benchmarks. Does that align?
[09:40] Lina Park: Yes.
[09:41] Samir Patel: Yep.
[09:42] Carlos Mendez: Timeline wise we'd like initial docs this week and a technical demo next week.
[09:47] Jordan Lee: We'll aim for docs by 4/28 and demo the week of 5/4.
[09:53] Priya Raman: I'll follow up with an invite for a 90-minute technical session.
[09:58] Maya Torres: Thank you.
[10:00] Jordan Lee: Thanks all — we'll send a recap and action items.
[10:05] Speaker 1: (End of recording)
